why_not_applied: shared_contracts/W01_TOOL_EVENT_CLASSIFIER.json is a FROZEN 028 artifact (classifier_id EXEC012-TOOL-EVENT-CLASSIFIER-028), sealed before amendment 030 and hash-covered by the 028 manifest. Amending it inside an evidence bundle would both misrepresent the contract that was in force during attempts 1-3 and diverge from the sealed original. It must be amended at the 028 surface under supervisor authority, as a versioned -031 classifier.
raised_by: PR #1341 review (P2, fail-closed gap). Not raised by any GitHub review thread.

defect.statement: The file declares policy = FAIL_CLOSED_ALLOWLIST and its policy_note states that anything not explicitly allowlisted is an unapproved native tool event. But verdict_contract enumerates only two outcomes -- on_any_forbidden_event and on_zero_forbidden_events. There is no explicit outcome for an event that is NEITHER allowlisted NOR on the forbidden list: a new or renamed envelope or item type from a future codex build.
defect.risk: A reader implementing to the verdict_contract alone would route an UNKNOWN item type into the on_zero_forbidden_events path and emit RUNTIME_TOOL_POLICY = PASS -- precisely the silent-pass that the stated policy exists to prevent. The prose forbids it; the machine-readable contract does not encode it.
defect.note_on_severity: This is a contract-text gap. It is NOT evidence that any run mis-classified anything -- see verified_behaviour below.

verified_behaviour_in_this_bundle.evidence: Across all ten live turns the only envelope types observed were thread.started, turn.started, item.completed and turn.completed, and the only item types were agent_message and reasoning. Every one is on the allowlist, so the unknown-event path was never exercised. UNAPPROVED_NATIVE_TOOL_EVENT_COUNT = 0 remains a true statement about these runs.
verified_behaviour_in_this_bundle.limitation: Because the path was never exercised, this bundle contains no evidence either way about what the implementations actually do with an unknown type. The gap is in the contract; whether the code fails closed is UNKNOWN from these artifacts and must be verified from source before the next dispatch.

fix_for_the_successor.change: Issue a -031 classifier adding an explicit third verdict branch.

on_any_unknown_event.applies_to: Any envelope type not in allowed_envelope_types and not in forbidden_envelope_types, or any item type not in allowed_item_types and not in forbidden_item_types.
on_any_unknown_event.rationale: Fail-closed allowlist. An unrecognised type is treated as unapproved, never as absence of tool use.

fix_for_the_successor.also: Tighten on_zero_forbidden_events so RUNTIME_TOOL_POLICY = PASS requires BOTH zero forbidden events AND zero unknown events.
fix_for_the_successor.verification_required_first: Read the classify_events implementation in Route A (W02/harness/adapter/core.py) and Route D (research_loop.py) and confirm each already rejects unknown types. If either silently ignores them, this is an implementation defect, not merely a contract gap, and its severity rises.
